chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasn al-Saffar narrated from 'Ibad ibn Sulayman, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him)
about Divine Unity, he responded: It is what you already follow.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا: Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (Imam Ali ibn Musa)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Divine Unity according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Rida (AS) defines Tawhid not as a complex theological construct but as the innate, foundational belief already held by the faithful, thereby countering anthropomorphic innovations. This response underscores the Shia emphasis on *Fitrah* (innate disposition) and the simplicity of core monotheism amidst scholarly elaboration. It serves as a reminder that true Tawhid is the baseline of Islamic identity rather than an esoteric secret.
